summary: Checked, in the order the verification page sets out. (1) Lookahead-scan on the final diff (git diff main...HEAD) reports exactly 2 findings, both shift(-1) at output_data_generic_exp_0/profile_inputs.py:37,47; both are information-coefficient diagnostics in a dev-window-only recon script that reads solely kapso_datasets/bars/ (780 rows per instrument, 2021-01-04..2023-12-29, zero 2024 rows) and is imported by nothing - changes.log lines 60-66 justifies them and the justification holds. strategy.py's own signal path scans clean. (2) The lookahead-auditor delegate returned PASS with evidence: truncation invariance over 108 cut points per instrument, single-bar perturbation over 30 bars per instrument (max |diff| at t<j = 0.000e+00, and bar j's own row moves in 30/30 cases, so there is no accidental second shift on top of the evaluator's own values.shift(1)), and the decisive dev-vs-full-frame test on the real 2021-2024 concatenated frame showing appending 2024 changes no dev-row position by a bit. All statistics in strategy.py are ewm or trailing rolling with fixed integer min_periods; no bfill, center=True, or whole-frame reduction. (3) Measurement trustworthy: I reproduced all three printed metrics independently from the evaluator's own recorded outputs - Sharpe 1.9335, max_drawdown 0.0117, turnover 8.4026 over 262 days all stamped 2024, max |position| 0.635, turnover column equals |delta position| to CSV rounding, and the first OOS bar's turnover is 0.012-0.039 rather than a spurious 1.0, confirming continuity across the boundary. The auditor re-ran the registered evaluation in an isolated copy and got byte-identical equity_curve.csv and trades.csv. Numbers are not impossible: 120 losing days of 262, 5 losing months of 12, ann vol 2.63% / ann return 5.09%, costs visibly charged (8.4 turnover x 5bp = 0.42%/yr), dev 2.1817 -> OOS 1.9336 an 11% give-back inside the ~0.98 standard error at n=262, and the edge concentrated in H2 2024 (Q1 -0.45, Q4 +3.91) - a fragility the notes state plainly rather than a bug. I re-ran dev_backtest.py myself and it reproduces the notes' dev figures exactly (2.1817 / 0.0188 / 8.5 / max|pos| 0.721). (4) No leakage: no file the attempt added references the OOS path in kapso_evaluation/private_dir.txt; the auditor found zero occurrences of that path and no 2024-dated CSV row in the attempt's session stream; the working tree is clean with no untracked cache. risk_line.py reads only results/equity_curve.csv, results/trades.csv and result.json - artifacts the domain statement says the evaluator writes and a hook asks sessions for - so it is not a read of the 2024 bars; it does surface 2024 quarterly detail, but strategy.py was written once before any evaluator output existed (commit c301244 at 11:27:49 precedes result.json at 11:28:52; strategy.py is touched by no later commit, one result.json, one scored run, days 262, fast=false), so no parameter came from the score, and experiment 2 was left unspent against a pre-registered PLAN.md fallback. kapso_evaluation/evaluate.py carries the identical blob c60b951 from the setup commit through HEAD - never modified in any commit - and the only change under that directory in the final diff is result.json, which the evaluator writes itself. Two open notes for the judge, neither voiding: the intermediate commit c301244 added a documentation file kapso_evaluation/eval_profile.md inside the protected directory and 7413059 git-mv'd it to the repo root after the attempt's own auditor flagged it, so HEAD is compliant, the evaluator and private_dir.txt were never altered and the measurement is unaffected - whether an intermediate commit into that directory matters is a rule call I leave visible rather than void on, since the attempt disclosed and fixed it; and the harness's evaluation_output.txt for this attempt is a mis-capture (it contains the session's closing chat message, not evaluator stdout), so I took the measurement from kapso_evaluation/result.json and output_data_generic_exp_0/eval_stdout.txt, which agree with each other and with my recomputation from the equity curve. The supplied diff.patch is complete but lacks a trailing newline, which makes git apply call it corrupt; its content is identical to git diff main...HEAD.
